# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Quinn Iverson**
[Street Address]
[City], NJ [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Wellpoint — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-14**
- **Member:** Quinn Iverson
- **Member ID:** W154693844
- **Reference number:** POC-E14E3A00BC-47205
- **Denied service:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey

---

## The policy I am asking you to apply

I am appealing under the plan's own published criteria: **Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)**, effective 11/05/2023, available at https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf. I am quoting only that guideline below, so that a reviewer can check each quotation against the source.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the total ankle replacement (CPT 27702) that my surgeon requested, and I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider and approve the procedure. The notice dated 2026-08-14 states that the records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. My records show that I completed a supervised course of conservative care well beyond the period the guideline requires, and my surgeon has documented that this surgery is needed.

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

The guideline states:

> "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present."

**Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken 2026-07-17 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.

**At least 3 months of supervised conservative management.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance for 16 weeks, from 2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That is more than five months of supervised care, against a requirement of three.

**Pain and functional impairment that persist after that care.** I have had 18 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. I took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 gave me only three weeks of partial relief. I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks. On examination, provocative testing is positive on the affected side and my range of motion is limited by pain.

**Vascular perfusion.** Please see [pedal pulse / vascular perfusion findings as documented in Dr. Okafor's examination note, with date] in the enclosed records.

**FDA-approved device.** The planned implant is [device name and manufacturer, as documented by Dr. Okafor], which is FDA approved.

The guideline also defines what counts as significant pain and functional impairment:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My difficulty walking is documented: an antalgic gait, with walking limited to two blocks. Please see [VAS pain score as recorded in Dr. Okafor's office notes, with date] and [second impacted daily activity as documented in the chart] for the remaining elements of this definition.

On the content of conservative care, the guideline states:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

> "• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records document not one but two of the listed complementary strategies: anti-inflammatory medication (NSAIDs for four months, with inadequate relief) and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05. They also document my compliance with a plan of therapy — 20 completed physical therapy visits over 16 weeks. If footwear modification or an accommodative device was also provided, those records are here as well: [dates and description of any footwear modification, padding or orthosis provided, as documented in the chart].

The guideline further states:

> "If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

and

> "If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable."

I want to be clear that I am not asking for an exception to conservative care. I did the conservative care. It was supervised, it was documented, and it did not relieve my pain.

Finally, the guideline describes how these criteria are meant to be applied:

> "Carelon applies objective and evidence-based criteria, and takes individual circumstances and the local delivery system into account when determining the medical appropriateness of health care services."

> "These criteria are designed to guide both providers and reviewers to the most appropriate services based on a patient's unique circumstances."

My circumstances are documented in the packet already submitted: 18 months of progressive pain, five months of supervised therapy, failed medication and injection, radiographs showing joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, and walking limited to two blocks. I also have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

## What I am asking Wellpoint to do

I respectfully ask that Wellpoint overturn the determination of 2026-08-14 (reference POC-E14E3A00BC-47205) and authorize the total ankle replacement, CPT 27702, as requested by Dr. Okafor. If the reviewer believes any single criterion above remains unmet, I ask that the decision identify that criterion specifically and tell me what document would satisfy it, so that my surgeon and I can supply it.

I understand that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, by **2027-02-10**. I am sending this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file or check on my appeal by logging in at anthem.com or through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card, and that my denial letter is the authoritative source for the deadline and the correct address.

Please send your decision in writing to the address above. I can be reached at [phone number] and [email address] if anything further is needed.

**Enclosures:** Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-14; physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14, 20 visits); weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-07-17; medication and injection records including corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-05; office notes from Okafor, MD; [any additional records listed here].

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

_____________________________
**Quinn Iverson**
Member ID: W154693844
[Date of birth]
[Phone] | [Email]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
